calibration_status: provisional and uncalibrated: constants chosen from rounding arithmetic and conventional practice; no real-paper calibration performed

implementation_agreement.compare_first: sample record_seq sets, N, then origin marginal effects; before any target comparison
implementation_agreement.two_of_three: If two implementations agree, score that pair and send the third to code audit. No agreeing pair: indeterminate (implementation_disagreement).

published_values.rounding: printed to 2 decimals: true value in [v - 0.005, v + 0.005]; printed p '0.00' means [0, 0.005); '-0.00' has negative sign with magnitude < 0.005
published_values.published_se: not printed in the article; SE-unit magnitude criterion is NOT audited
published_values.implied_se_diagnostic: SE implied by printed marginal effect and printed p (two-sided normal) computed with interval arithmetic as a separate publication diagnostic; never used for a verdict

criteria.sign: Mismatch only if the reconstructed estimate lies outside the published rounding interval and has the opposite sign of the published value (published 0.00 has no sign).
criteria.inference_rule: Published band set = bands overlapping the published p rounding interval. Band distance = minimum index distance between published and reconstructed bands. For a claim of significance in the hypothesized direction, a stronger reconstructed band is not a failure. Distance 1 is never sufficient for discrepancy; a weaker band by 2 or more is an inference failure. A reconstructed result significant at 0.10 where the article reports p >= 0.10 is recorded as contradicting nonsignificance.
criteria.tail: two-sided, normal reference, as the article reports two-sided robust p values (both readers; A assumed two)
criteria.hypothesized_direction: negative for hierarchy coefficients (article's stated finding)
criteria.magnitude: SE-unit magnitude not audited (no published SEs). Report absolute difference, whether the reconstruction lies within the printed rounding interval, and relative difference, labelled as printed-precision descriptives.

benchmark_inference.rule: assignment-level clustered sandwich. The hierarchy regressor is assigned at the group level (captured cohort or camp), which equals the native clustering; benchmark = native. Captured-cohort models also report camp clustering as an uncertain alternative, not as benchmark.
benchmark_inference.below_threshold: inference not audited for that model (no nonlinear wild bootstrap is specified)

equivalent_set: Origin only: reconciliation produced no substantive alternative labelled equivalent by both readers. Specification fragility is therefore NOT assessed; one-at-a-time uncertain branches are reported separately with sign agreement, share significant at 0.05 and 0.10 in the hypothesized direction, median and range.
label_sensitivity: If replacing the origin by any uncertain branch would change a claim's outcome category between consistent and potential discrepancy, flag label_sensitive and keep both.

outcomes.consistent: implementations agree; origin sign criterion passes and inference band distance <= 1 or stronger; magnitude criterion not audited (stated); equivalent set = origin
outcomes.fragile_inference: not applicable unless benchmark differs from native; benchmark equals native here
outcomes.potential_discrepancy: implementations agree and origin fails sign or inference (>= 2 bands weaker) criterion
outcomes.discrepant: potential discrepancy that survives adversarial review and actual human confirmation; adversarial review cannot use a model family independent of both implementation families (none available), so no fully verified discrepancy can be claimed in this session
outcomes.indeterminate: sub-codes: implementation_disagreement, inference_unaudited_few_clusters, within_claim_mixed, label_sensitive, source_vintage, underdocumentation
outcomes.not_attemptable: core source absent or fit impossible

grey_zone: benefit of uncertainty goes to indeterminate

n_branch.rule: computed by code: match if |N_rec - N_pub| / N_pub <= 0.005; otherwise record N mismatch and its size; N mismatch qualifies coverage but does not by itself change the outcome category
n_branch.use: never used to choose a sample

claim_aggregation: A Table 4 claim (measure x group type) has two coefficients (simple and full). Consistent if both consistent; potential discrepancy if both are; otherwise indeterminate:within_claim_mixed.

paper_aggregation.focal: four Table 4 claims (Steepness-captured, Steepness-camp, Sameness-captured, Sameness-camp)
paper_aggregation.mapping: fully reproduced: all four consistent and no lower tier potential discrepancy; partially reproduced: all four consistent with a discrepant lower tier; not reproduced: all four discrepant; indeterminate: any focal claim indeterminate; other combinations (mixed consistent/discrepant focal) reported as 'not covered by mapping: focal mixed' with counts
paper_aggregation.label_sensitivity: repeat with the four Table 6 interaction claims added as focal (Table 6 focal status uncertain)
paper_aggregation.lower_tiers: Table 5 Panel A, Table 5 ROC and text-only robustness claims are scored descriptively (sign and significance counts against the article's statement) and can qualify but not determine the paper outcome

data_regime: same provider and file series as the article (NARA RG 389 POW file and RG 64 enlistment file); the article's vintage/download date is unknown; camp geocoding and rank mapping independently constructed
